en: The Praise of the Jewel-King Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled *Daśabhūmīśvara*,
for those who delight in tranquility and self-control, whose intentions are peaceful and subdued, who are like the path of birds, and who are equal to the sky.
Listen to the supreme distinction of those who have shaken off the impurities of the hindrances, who abide in the knowledge of the path, and who are the most excellent Bodhisattvas. || 1 ||
Having accumulated a hundred thousand merits over ten million eons, and having honored hundreds of thousands of excellent Buddhas, he has taken up [this vow];
indeed, having honored infinite Pratyekabuddhas, the most excellent of Jinas.
The thought of awakening arises for the benefit of the entire world. || 2 ||
Moreover, [I pay homage] to those who have scorched their afflictions, who have reached the perfection of patience,
whose conduct is rooted in what is beneficial, and who have arisen from merit and wisdom;
to those whose movement is vast and whose intentions are directed toward merit and wisdom.
The thought of awakening arises as equal to the ten powers. || 3 ||
To those who are joyful and wise, who delight in the dharma of giving,
who are constantly exerted for the sake of the welfare of the entire world,
who take pleasure in the qualities of the Victors, and who are devoted to the vow of protecting sentient beings—
The thought of awakening arises, which brings about the welfare of the three worlds. || 4 ||
To those who have desisted from unwholesome deeds, who stand upon the pure path, who delight in vows and observances, whose faculties are peaceful and gentle,
who have gone for refuge to the Victor, and whose intention is the practice of awakening—
The thought of awakening (bodhicitta), which accomplishes the welfare of the three worlds, is born. || 5 ||
To those who have followed after the wholesome, who possess a natural inclination toward patience, who have discerned the flavor of virtue, who have abandoned the festival of pride,
whose noble minds are firmly established, and whose intentions are gentle through generosity—
The generation of the mind of awakening (bodhicitta) brings about the accomplishment of the welfare of all beings. || 6 ||
When he sets out for a virtuous deed, steadfast heroes become his companions for the sake of the welfare of all people; Mānasiṃha exerts himself,
achieving ceaseless virtues and conquering the host of afflictions.
Instantly, the thought of awakening arises in their minds.
Those whose minds are well-composed, who have destroyed the darkness of delusion, whose pride and conceit have dissolved, who have abandoned the defiled path,
and who delight in equanimity having renounced attachment to saṃsāra— [to them I bow].
Instantly, the thought of awakening arises in their minds.
With minds as pure as space, having destroyed the Māra Namuci through wisdom and discernment, having vomited out afflictions and pride,
they abide in the refuge of the Victor’s feet, having attained the body of ultimate reality.
Instantly, the thought of awakening arises in their minds. || 9 ||

Those who are steadfast in the wisdom of the means for accomplishing the welfare of the three worlds; those who possess the increase of skill in the means for removing the power of their enemies; and those who, through their devotion to merit, strive for the qualities of the Sugata—[may they be victorious].
Instantly, the thought of awakening arises in their minds. || 10 ||
Those Bodhisattvas who, desiring the welfare of the three worlds and with minds resolved for the fulfillment of the accumulations of enlightenment, engage even in difficult practices;
they are those who are ever-vigilant in virtuous deeds and exulting in their progress.
Instantly, the thought of awakening (bodhicitta) arises in their minds. || 11 ||
Desiring the qualities of the Ten Powers, devoted to the conduct of awakening, having conquered the flood of the elephant-like force [of the senses], and having abandoned attachment to pride;
they have followed the auspicious path and attained the goals of Dharma, Artha, and Kāma.
Instantly, the thought of awakening arises in their minds. || 12 ||
Thus, may those who possess the qualities of calculation practice the conduct of awakening;
may they attain the true prosperity of the vows for the state of a Victor;
and may those purified throughout the three worlds attain the mind of awakening.
May the bodhisattvas be completely purified through the three refuges. 13.
Having fulfilled the ten perfections, one becomes a lord of the ten stages;
this is further explained, so listen now to it in brief. (14)
When one, having attained the thought of awakening (bodhicitta), performs the act of giving, then, having reached the stage of Perfect Joy (pramuditā), one becomes a lord of Jambūdvīpa. || 15 ||
Abiding therein, one should protect sentient beings by providing for them according to their wishes;
having established oneself in generosity, one should also enjoin others to do so. (16)
Having established all beings in awakening and having reached the perfection of complete generosity,
one should undertake the vow through the power of this karma.
Having established himself in the precepts of restraint and being virtuous, he shall thereafter attain the stainless state and become a sovereign lord of the four continents. || 18 ||
Established therein, he should protect sentient beings and restrain them from unwholesome deeds;
having himself become established in ethical discipline, he should also enjoin others to it. (19)
Having established all beings in enlightenment, one becomes perfected in virtue;
through the ripening of this dharma, one should take recourse in the vow of patience. || 20 ||
Having properly maintained the vow of patience, one who possesses patience shall become virtuous;
thereafter, having attained the Radiant realm, he becomes the sovereign of the Heaven of the Thirty-three. || 21 ||
Established therein, he should protect sentient beings by warding off the path of afflictions;
remaining himself in the vow of patience, he should also engage others in it. (22)
Having established sentient beings in awakening, one shall reach the further shore of peace;
by the ripening of this merit, one shall rely upon the power of vigor. (23)
Having correctly applied right effort, one who possesses vigor becomes skilled;
then, having attained the Arciṣmatī stage, he becomes a lord of the nectar of immortality.
Remaining there and protecting all [beings], he should restrain those with wrong views;
having established them in right view, he should awaken them through diligent effort. (25)
Having personally established oneself in the vow of meditation, one should also engage others in it;
having settled all beings in awakening, one becomes one who has reached the further shore of meditation. (26)
Through the ripening of this merit, one should undertake the perfection of meditative concentration;
having completely conquered all afflictions, one shall become firmly established in samādhi. || 27 ||
Having attained right meditation, one becomes skilled in concentration;
then, having reached the stage of Sudurjaya, one becomes the lord of the Tuṣita heaven. || 28 ||
Remaining there, he should protect sentient beings by warding off the paths of the heretics; having established them in the Dharma of sentient beings, he should diligently awaken them. (29)
Having established oneself in the vow of meditation, one should also enjoin others to it;
having established all beings in awakening, one becomes one who has reached the further shore of meditation. || 30 ||
By the ripening of this merit, one shall take recourse in the vow of wisdom;
having completely conquered all Māras, one will possess the perfection of wisdom and the superknowledges.
Having correctly concentrated right wisdom, one becomes skilled in one's own superknowledges; then, having attained the Abhimukhī stage, one becomes a lord of the Sunirmita heaven. || 32 ||
Abiding there, one should protect sentient beings by removing their conceit, having firmly established them in emptiness and having awakened them through diligent effort. (33)
Having established oneself in the vow of wisdom, one should also enjoin others to it;
having settled all beings in awakening, one becomes one who has reached the further shore of wisdom. || 34 ||
Through the ripening of this merit, one should practice the vow of skillful means;
having completely conquered all the wicked, the wise person becomes proficient in the true Dharma. (35)
By means of the application of skillful methods, one should establish sentient beings in enlightenment;
then, having reached the stage of Dūraṅgamā, one becomes a sovereign lord who possesses mastery. || 36 ||
Abiding there, one should protect sentient beings by means of realizations and awakenings;
having established them in the fixed course of the bodhisattvas, one should bring them to full enlightenment.
Having established oneself therein in skillful means, one should also engage others;
having established all beings in awakening, one becomes one who has reached the further shore of skillful means. || 38 ||
And by the power of this merit, one should rely upon excellent vows;
having utterly conquered false views, right view has been established by the wise. (39)
With a well-established mind, he was firmly established in perfect awakening;
thereafter, the lord of a thousand [worlds] attained immovability through his intellect. (40)
Remaining there, he should protect sentient beings and slowly drink the three nectars;
having established them in the thorough knowledge of the world-system, he should awaken them.
Having established oneself in the supreme vow, one should also enjoin others to it;
having established all beings in enlightenment, one becomes a master who has reached the further shore.
In accordance with these merits, one who is resolved upon perfect enlightenment should undertake the vow of power after having utterly conquered all evil forces. (43)
Through right effort and great exertion, one shall utterly defeat all the non-Buddhist teachers;
then, having reached the stage of Sādhumatī, the accomplished one becomes a Great Brahmā.

Remaining there, protecting sentient beings through instructions on the vehicle of the Buddha, he should awaken them to the perfect enlightenment that consists in the thorough knowledge of the equality of all beings. (45)
Having established oneself in power, one should also enjoin others [to do so];
having established all beings in awakening, one becomes one who has reached the further shore of power. || 46 ||
And through the ripening of this merit, one should take recourse in the vow of knowledge;
having utterly conquered the four Māras, one becomes a mine of the qualities of a Bodhisattva. (47)
Having established right knowledge, one should become skilled in the true Dharma;
then, having attained the Cloud of Dharma, the accomplished one becomes a Great Lord (Maheśvara).
Abiding there, protecting all beings through the awakening to all aspects, he should establish them in the supreme knowledge of all aspects and bring them to full enlightenment. 49.
Having established oneself in knowledge, one should also engage others;
having established all beings in awakening, one shall reach the further shore of knowledge. || 50 ||
And by the power of this merit, may the Jina, the Lord of the ten stages, the support of all qualities in every aspect, the omniscient one who has attained the Dharma, [be realized]. 51.
Thinking thus, with focused minds, one should practice the ten perfections in order to attain the state of a perfectly awakened Buddha. (52)
Likewise, having attained auspicious awakening, you shall utterly conquer the four Māras;
and having established all beings in awakening, you shall attain final liberation. 53.
Having understood this, practice within the shadow [of the teaching] in the doctrine of awakening;
having attained unimpeded awakening, may you obtain the state of the Sugata. || 54 ||

The Son of the Conqueror has indeed thus briefly explained these ten bodhisattva stages; they should be regarded as being endowed with the excellence of all aspects and followed by all forms of gnosis. At that moment, this trichiliocosm shook in six ways, various flowers fell from the sky, and divine and human beings broke into a chorus of praise.
And by means of a portion of that rejoicing, the realm as far as the Akaniṣṭha heaven was made manifest.
The *Stotra* on the Jewel-King of Mahāyāna Sūtras entitled *Daśabhūmīśvara*, from the *Śrī-bodhisattvacaryā-prasthāna*, is completed.
